lessons.title: Present simple: he, she, it
lessons.explain: When the subject is he, she or it, the verb in the present simple takes -s or -es. One person or thing works the same way.
lessons.intro: Good morning, everyone! Today we are learning the present simple with he, she and it. Look at the board: she plays cricket every day. Because the subject is she, the verb gets an s.

steps.question: Which sentence is correct?
options: She is play cricket every day.
steps.why: With she, the present simple verb takes -s, so play becomes plays.

steps.question: Say this sentence correctly.
steps.wrong: My brother go to school by bus.
answers: My brother goes to school by bus.
steps.why: My brother is he, so go becomes goes.

steps.question: Fill the gap: The sun ___ in the east.
steps.why: The sun is it, so rise becomes rises.

steps.question: Which verb needs -es instead of -s?
steps.why: Verbs ending in ch, sh, s, x or o take -es: watch becomes watches.

steps.question: Tell me one thing your best friend does every morning.

lessons.outro: Well done, class! Remember: with he, she and it, the verb takes an s.

lessons.title: Past simple: finished actions
lessons.explain: Use the past simple for actions that are finished, like yesterday or last week. Many verbs add -ed. Some change completely: go becomes went.
lessons.intro: Hello, class! Today's topic is the past simple. When we talk about yesterday or last week, the verb changes. Play becomes played, and go becomes went.

steps.question: Which sentence is correct?
options: Yesterday I go to the park.
Yesterday I went to the park.
Yesterday I going to the park.
Yesterday I goes to the park.
steps.why: Yesterday is finished time, so go becomes went.

steps.question: Say this sentence correctly.
steps.wrong: Last week we visit our grandmother.
answers: Last week we visited our grandmother.
We visited our grandmother last week.
steps.why: Last week is in the past, so visit becomes visited.

steps.question: What is the past simple of see?
steps.why: See is irregular: in the past simple it becomes saw.

steps.question: Fill the gap: She ___ her homework last night.
steps.why: Last night is finished time, so finish takes -ed.

steps.question: Tell me about something you did last Sunday.

lessons.outro: Great work today! For finished time, use the past form of the verb.

lessons.title: A or an?
lessons.explain: Use an before a vowel sound: an apple, an hour. Use a before a consonant sound: a book, a university. Listen to the sound, not the letter.
lessons.intro: Good morning! Today we will learn when to say a and when to say an. Listen to the first sound of the next word. Apple starts with a vowel sound, so we say an apple.

steps.question: Which one is correct?
steps.why: Engineer starts with a vowel sound, so we say an engineer.

steps.question: Which phrase is correct?
steps.why: The h in hour is silent, so hour starts with a vowel sound: an hour.

steps.question: Say this sentence correctly.
steps.wrong: I saw a elephant at the zoo.
answers: I saw an elephant at the zoo.
steps.why: Elephant starts with a vowel sound, so a becomes an.

steps.question: Tell me about an animal you like. Use a or an in your sentence.

lessons.outro: Wonderful! Listen to the first sound: a before consonant sounds, an before vowel sounds.
